native.title: Day / Night
native.description: IR-cut switching mode and the photocell knobs that gate it.

native.title: Image adjustment
native.description: Picture sliders, orientation and exposure. Option lists are read live from the camera — fields the firmware doesn't expose are hidden.

native.title: Main stream
native.description: Encoder parameters pushed to the camera. Option lists are read live from the camera — fields the firmware doesn't expose are hidden.

native.title: Sub stream
native.description: Encoder parameters pushed to the camera. Option lists are read live from the camera — fields the firmware doesn't expose are hidden.

fields.label: Threshold
fields.description: Pixel intensity difference to count as changed (higher = less sensitive)

fields.label: Min Subject Size
fields.description: Smallest subject that triggers motion, as a share of the analysed view. Fragments of one subject are merged before this is applied, so a partly hidden animal counts once at its full size. Only in effect when Min Area is 0.

fields.label: Min Area
fields.description: Absolute pixel bar, applied to each motion region on its own. This is how motion has always worked, and it stays the default. Set it to 0 to move THIS camera to Min Subject Size, which merges the fragments of one subject before measuring it and keeps its meaning at any resolution - expect more motion, so move one camera at a time.

fields.label: Storm Cutoff
fields.description: A merged region whose changed pixels cover more of the view than this is weather, an IR cut or an exposure step, not a subject, and does not fire motion. A real mover inside the storm still fires on its own region. Only in effect when Min Area is 0; 1 disables the cutoff.

fields.label: Blur Radius
fields.description: Gaussian blur before diff (reduces noise)

fields.label: Dilation Radius
fields.description: Expand motion regions to merge nearby changes

fields.label: Preferred stream
fields.description: Stream used when grabbing a snapshot

fields.label: Max cache age (s)
fields.description: Serve cached snapshot up to this age before re-capturing. Default 15s for non-battery cams (live-feel). The UI refresh button always forces a fresh capture regardless of this value.

fields.label: Debug logging
fields.description: Log stream selection and timing details for this device.

reolinkBattery.title: Scheduled refresh
reolinkBattery.description: How often this battery camera is guaranteed to have been read, so a battery level never goes stale unseen.

fields.label: Refresh window (min)
fields.description: Once per window this camera refreshes everything CamStack knows about it — battery level and charging, signal, device info, every state panel and the cached snapshot. If the camera is awake at some point in the window (a motion event, a live view, anything that woke it) it is refreshed then and not woken again; if the whole window passes with the camera asleep, it is woken ONCE near the end of the window, refreshed, and left to go back to sleep. A camera that does not answer is retried at most twice per window. 15–240 minutes, default 60; 0 turns the scheduled refresh off (the battery level then ages until the camera next wakes by itself).

fields.label: Motion detection
fields.description: Master switch for the camera's on-board motion detector. Disabling stops the camera from emitting motion events on the alarm channel.

fields.label: Sensitivity
fields.description: Higher = triggers on smaller motion. Reolink user-facing range 1..50.

options.label: Camera sensors
options.description: The camera's own motion, plus any sensor attached to it

options.label: Device activity (the device says it is working)
This node (ML root step on decoded frames)
Camera onboard AI (replaces the root step when picked alone)

fields.label: Motion Cooldown
fields.description: Time without a fresh motion event before the active phase ends. Applies to all motion sources — every motion event re-arms the timer.

fields.label: Max session hold
fields.description: Upper bound on how long detection keeps running past the motion cooldown while a subject is still moving in-frame but no longer triggering motion. Prevents the detection box from stopping on a slow-moving subject. Set to 0 to disable.

fields.label: Audio window after motion
fields.description: How long audio keeps being analysed after the last motion event. Each new motion event extends the window without restarting the audio stream.

fields.label: Run motion analyzer on onboard motion
fields.description: When onboard motion is detected, temporarily start the frame-diff analyzer to emit zone results. Stops after the motion cooldown window.

fields.label: Occupancy re-check
fields.description: Periodically re-sample a few frames during the watching phase, so objects that are simply parked are still counted (motion gating alone loses them after a restart). On by default at a wide interval; turn it off on cameras where the extra decoder re-dial is expensive.

orchestrator.title: Object Detection
orchestrator.description: When the SW object detection pipeline (yolov9s, scrfd, …) runs for this camera. Wrappers stay bound regardless — the runner reads this mode at attach time to decide whether to pull the substream.

fields.label: Detection FPS
fields.description: Maximum frames decoded and sent to object detection each second

fields.label: Detection FPS while the device is working
fields.description: A device-activity session lasts as long as the job does — a cleaning run is tens of minutes. This caps the rate for that session only; a session opened by motion keeps the rate above.

orchestrator.title: Audio classification
orchestrator.description: When the audio classifier (apple-soundanalysis, etc.) runs for this camera. Default for battery cams: disabled (continuous audio holds the substream open).

fields.label: Audio stream
fields.description: Which camera stream the audio classifier listens on. Auto picks the lowest stream the camera serves natively — a transcoded stream is never started just to hear a camera.

orchestrator.title: Occupancy
orchestrator.description: Periodic re-sampling to keep stationary objects / occupancy fresh while the camera is idle (watching).

fields.label: Occupancy re-check interval
fields.description: How often (in seconds) the runner re-samples a few frames to confirm the scene is truly empty during the watching phase.

fields.label: Occupancy re-check frames
fields.description: Number of frames sampled per occupancy re-check burst.

orchestrator.title: Pre-roll detection
orchestrator.description: When motion opens a session the camera has already buffered a few seconds of footage. Detecting over it finds a subject at the moment it appeared instead of after the decoder has warmed up.

fields.label: Detect in the pre-roll
fields.description: Run detection over the few seconds of footage the camera had already buffered when motion fired, so a subject that was in view before the trigger is found at the moment it appeared rather than seconds later. The burst is bounded and never delays live detection.

fields.label: Pre-roll frames
fields.description: How many frames of buffered history may be detected on, per session. Higher samples the history more densely; 0 disables the pass.

fields.label: Pipeline Node
fields.description: Which node runs the detection pipeline for this camera.

fields.label: Debug media
fields.description: Off (the default) keeps first/last frame, key frames, thumbnails and face/plate crops, and reduces motion-only stills to one marker per detection drought. On also stores the per-track filmstrip and a still on EVERY motion transition — diagnostic volume, roughly 95 KiB per transition.

fields.label: Motion marker after
fields.description: With debug media off: a motion still is kept only when no detection has run on this camera for this long, and at most one per window. Fleet p90 of detection-free stretches is ~13 min.

fields.label: Snapshot interval
fields.description: How often a snapshot is persisted per active track.

fields.label: Snapshot movement gate
fields.description: After the interval elapses, only capture a snapshot if the object moved this fraction of the frame since the last one. Higher = fewer near-identical frames. 0 disables the gate.

fields.label: Snapshot max idle
fields.description: Force a snapshot for a stationary but still-present track after this long without one, so its filmstrip is never empty.

analytics.title: Audio metrics reporting
analytics.description: Coalesce audio-metrics state updates so the events tab + bus aren't flooded by per-second dBFS jitter on idle scenes. Per-camera override.

fields.label: Mirror to device-state
fields.description: When off, the audio classifier still runs (the live AUDIO METRICS panel reads through the cap method), but the periodic state-changed events are suppressed. Use for cameras where audio is informational only.

fields.label: Report threshold
fields.description: Minimum dBFS delta between consecutive snapshots to trigger an emit. 2dB means quiet noise jitter (±1dB) is suppressed; class changes always emit regardless. Lower = more updates.

analytics.title: Retention
analytics.description: ONE window per camera. Everything this camera produces — tracks, their events, media, faces, plates and search vectors, plus motion, audio and sensor events — is deleted on it. Default: as long as the camera's recordings, so footage and analytics stay one policy. Enrolled faces and plates are never pruned.

fields.label: Mode
fields.description: Follow recordings: history lives exactly as long as retained footage (age retention AND disk eviction; never prunes the last 7 days). Custom: the window below.

fields.label: Window
fields.description: How long this camera's analytics history is kept in Custom mode — and the bound in Follow mode when the camera has no footage at all. 0 = keep forever, which switches retention OFF for this camera entirely (motion and audio events included, and those grow by thousands of rows a day).

analytics.title: Package detection
analytics.description: Detect a delivered package (a package-class object left parked inside a package zone) and, symmetrically, its pick-up. Draw the package zone in the zone editor; enable the package class in the object-detection step. Per-device override.

fields.label: Enable package detection
fields.description: Turn package delivered / picked-up detection on for this camera (off elsewhere).

fields.label: Emit pick-up
fields.description: Also emit a package-picked-up event when the delivered package leaves.

fields.label: Early pick-up
fields.description: Report a pick-up as soon as the package detector has looked three times over at least 10 s, found the spot empty and unblocked, and somebody was in the drop-off zone — instead of after 5 minutes without a sighting. Off by default until it is measured on more pick-ups.

fields.label: Confirmation frames
fields.description: How many frames the box must be seen on before it counts as a delivery. One is a flicker; two can still be a passer-by; three is the default bar against false positives. Independent of dwell.

fields.label: Minimum dwell
fields.description: Extra time the package must stay parked after the confirmation frames. 0 (default) means N frames is enough — a courier who drops and leaves in a couple of seconds still delivers. Raise to reject a bag briefly set down.

fields.label: Minimum package size
fields.description: Reject tiny far-field blobs: the package box must cover at least this fraction of the frame.

fields.label: Maximum package size
fields.description: Reject scene-sized blobs: a "package" covering more of the frame than this is scenery (a light patch, a doormat), not a parcel. Real parcels measure 1–2% of the frame; the recurring false positive measured 8–9.5%. This — not confidence — is the lever against a static false positive.

fields.label: Deliverer window
fields.description: A delivery only counts if a person or vehicle was in the configured package drop-off zone within this many seconds before the package appeared — and a pick-up only with somebody in that zone when it vanished. Motion elsewhere on the camera does not count. 0 disables the requirement.

analytics.title: Audio detection
analytics.description: Thresholds for audio-level and classification events. Per-device override.

fields.label: Classification min score
fields.description: Minimum confidence (0–1) for a classification result to be accepted.

fields.label: Event classes
fields.description: Which sounds may become an event on this camera. Leave empty to allow every class. The classifier is untouched — it keeps hearing and labelling everything; this only narrows what is worth an event and a notification here.

fields.label: Occurrences to confirm
fields.description: How many times the same sound must be heard inside the window below before it becomes an event. 1 disables the window — every occurrence is an event.

fields.label: Confirmation window
fields.description: Width of the corroboration window. Occurrences are counted per class, so two different sounds never confirm each other. Ignored when occurrences is 1.

fields.label: Level deviation
fields.description: dB above the rolling mean required to trigger a peak event.

fields.label: Level window
fields.description: Rolling baseline window length for peak detection.

fields.label: Level max wait
fields.description: Maximum silence between events before a heartbeat sample is emitted.

analytics.title: Audio markers
analytics.description: A synthetic timeline marker (with a snapshot) for audio that is out of the ordinary FOR THIS CAMERA, loud, and heard while nothing visual is happening. Off by default: leave it off for a day and read the “audio anomaly gate (window)” log line — its `wouldFire` count is how many markers this camera would have produced, per camera, before you pay for any of them.

fields.label: Create audio markers
fields.description: When off the criteria are still evaluated and counted (wouldFire) — only the marker is not created.

fields.label: Baseline window
fields.description: How much of its own history defines this camera’s “normal” loudness. Also the warm-up: no marker until this much audio has been heard.

fields.label: Minimum volume
fields.description: Absolute loudness floor. A sound quieter than this is never a marker, however unusual it is for the camera. 0 dBFS is digital full scale, so this is negative.

fields.label: Out-of-the-ordinary factor
fields.description: How many multiples of this camera’s OWN loudness jitter the sound must exceed. A camera on a busy road needs a bigger jump than one in a garden — that is the point of measuring it per camera.

fields.label: Minimum jump
fields.description: Floor, in dB, on how far above its own normal the sound must sit. Holds when a camera is so steady that the factor above would pass on any nudge.

fields.label: Motion-quiet window
fields.description: Suppress the marker if a track was alive or motion was reported within this long. An audio marker laid over an active track is noise.

fields.label: Minimum gap
fields.description: Shortest interval between two markers on this camera.

fields.label: Ceiling per hour
fields.description: Hard burst ceiling per camera. Drops past it are counted, not silent.

fields.label: Ceiling per day
fields.description: Hard daily ceiling per camera — this, not the thresholds, is what bounds the worst case. A mis-tuned threshold can only ever cost you this many markers a day.

analytics.title: Audio episodes
analytics.description: One timeline track and one event per classified sound, held open with hysteresis so a long cry is not four tracks. No class filter: speech, crying, a bark — the knobs below are what stop repeats. Leave on for a day or two and judge the spam, then tighten per camera.

fields.label: Create audio episodes
fields.description: Off switches off the GROUPING only: classified audio still persists an event and still notifies, but no timeline track is opened and a long sound is no longer collapsed into one episode (one event per class change, then one every 5 s while it lasts).

fields.label: Open hold
fields.description: The class must be heard continuously this long before an episode opens. Filters 200 ms blips.

fields.label: Close gap
fields.description: The class must be absent this long before the episode closes. A pause inside a cry does not start a second track.

fields.label: Cooldown
fields.description: After an episode closes, the same class cannot reopen until this elapses.

analytics.title: Face recognition
analytics.description: How a face is matched to a person. Which cameras look for faces is set per camera, in its detection steps. The switch turns matching off everywhere; the other values can also be set per camera.

fields.label: Similarity threshold
fields.description: How alike (0–1) a face must be to a known person to be matched. Higher = stricter. Near misses (from 80% of this value) are offered as suggestions.

fields.label: Ambiguity margin
fields.description: The best match must beat the second best by at least this much, or the face stays unassigned.

fields.label: Min face size to keep (px)
fields.description: Faces smaller than this (short side, full-resolution pixels) are dropped and not stored. Applied after the embedding floor in Faces & recognition.

fields.label: Min face size to auto-assign (px)
fields.description: Stored faces smaller than this (short side, full-resolution pixels) can be assigned by hand but are never matched automatically — small faces give wrong matches. Raise it if distant faces get the wrong name.

fields.label: Min identity samples
fields.description: A person needs at least this many saved faces before new faces are matched to them automatically.

fields.label: Confirm frames
fields.description: Frames an identity must be seen before a track is assigned. Minimum 1.

fields.label: Max embedding magnitude (0 = off)
fields.description: Reject a face whose embedding is abnormally strong — a blank or garbled crop that would match everyone. Leave at 0 until the "face: embedding magnitude" log lines show where your cameras sit.

fields.label: Buffer max per device
fields.description: Maximum buffered face entries kept per device.

fields.label: Keep the source frame of every buffered face
fields.description: Also store the whole frame each face came from (about 1.6 MB at 4K), so faces can be re-extracted later with a better model. Off by default.

analytics.title: Detection sensitivity
analytics.description: Per-device tracking and event-emission tuning. Lower values produce more events; higher values suppress noise.

fields.label: Min track age
fields.description: Minimum tracker hits before a track is exposed to the event emitter.

fields.label: Event cooldown
fields.description: Minimum seconds between repeated events for the same track.

fields.label: Min detection hits
fields.description: Minimum consecutive detection hits before a track is promoted to output.

fields.label: Stationary threshold
fields.description: Seconds without significant movement before a track is marked stationary.

analytics.title: Confirmation gate
analytics.description: Before a NEW track is born, re-run object detection on the hi-res native crop of the detection box. If the crop does not confirm a compatible object above the threshold, the birth is suppressed as a false positive. Fail-DEFERRED: a crop miss, unavailable inference, or a timeout leaves the birth UNDECIDED and looks again on later frames — it is not confirmed by default. Only an exhausted deferral with no crop at all lets a birth through unmeasured.

fields.label: Confirm new tracks
fields.description: Re-detect the native crop before a birth. Off = every track is born from the low-res detection frame directly.

fields.label: Min confirmation score
fields.description: Minimum re-detection score (0..1) required in the crop, class-compatible with the track, for a birth to be confirmed.

fields.label: Min crop size
fields.description: Subject boxes smaller than this (longest side, detection-frame px) are too tiny to confirm reliably — the gate defers them and looks again as the subject approaches and the box grows. 0 = confirm every birth regardless of size.

fields.label: Confirmation timeout
fields.description: Per-ATTEMPT budget for crop fetch + re-detection. If it does not resolve in time the attempt ends undecided, so the frame path never stalls on inference.

fields.label: Max deferral
fields.description: How long an undecided birth may wait for a native crop before the gate decides on the sub-native fallback. Measured from the first attempt, so retries cannot push it out. 0 = decide on the first attempt.

fields.label: Max gate attempts
fields.description: How many times one birth may be put through the gate, the first attempt included. The deferral ends on this or on the max deferral, whichever comes first.

analytics.title: Tracking
analytics.description: Per-device tracker tuning: association, coasting, spawn floors, sub-floor continuation and detector-dropout handling. Use the deviceId-tagged logs (track started/lost/ended, frame processed) to measure the effect.

fields.label: IoU match threshold
fields.description: Overlap required to match a (predicted) track to a detection. Higher = stricter.

fields.label: Max coasting time
fields.description: How long (ms) a track may miss detections before it is dropped. Time-based so it behaves the same on a 5fps and a 23fps camera.

fields.label: Min track age
fields.description: A track must exist for at least this long (ms) before it can produce events — stops sub-second flicker fragments from becoming events.

fields.label: Predictive coasting
fields.description: Extrapolate a coasting track by its velocity so a moved object re-matches instead of spawning a duplicate.

fields.label: Class-consistent matching
fields.description: Only match a detection to a track of the same class.

fields.label: Duplicate-track suppression
fields.description: Suppress and merge concurrent duplicate tracks. Stops one subject the detector double-fires (two boxes for one object, or a person misdetected as an animal) from becoming several time-overlapping tracks that each fire their own event. Off = legacy behaviour.

fields.label: Duplicate spawn IoU
fields.description: Overlap at/above which a NEW track is treated as a duplicate of a concurrent same-kind track and not created. High so two distinct subjects appearing close together are still tracked separately.

fields.label: Person/animal duplicate merge
fields.description: Treat an animal track overlapping a person track as the same subject (a person in a crouching / bending pose is often misdetected as an animal). The person track wins.

fields.label: Animal-over-person max score
fields.description: A low-confidence animal detection (score below this) sitting on a concurrent person track is suppressed — the common person-in-odd-pose false animal.

fields.label: Animal-over-person IoU
fields.description: Overlap with a concurrent person track that triggers the low-confidence animal spawn suppression.

fields.label: Detector-dropout skip
fields.description: Skip frames where detections suddenly drop to zero (likely a detector glitch) to protect coasting tracks.

fields.label: Dropout max skip frames
fields.description: Max consecutive all-zero frames absorbed as a glitch before the scene is treated as genuinely empty.

fields.label: Per-track class voting
fields.description: Report a track’s class by a confidence-weighted majority over its whole life instead of the latest frame — a person read as an animal on a single crouch/bend frame keeps the person label.

fields.label: Class-vote min fraction
fields.description: The winning class must hold at least this fraction of a track’s total vote weight to override the latest frame; below it the latest frame wins (so a genuine mid-life reclassification is not frozen out).

fields.label: Per-class spawn confidence
fields.description: Require a per-class minimum detection score before a NEW track is created. Kills static-object / reflection false spawns from the FP-prone classes. An already-tracked object still matches on a low-confidence frame.

fields.label: Min spawn score — person
fields.description: Minimum score to spawn a person track. 0 keeps person fully sensitive.

fields.label: Min spawn score — animal
fields.description: Minimum score to spawn an animal track (FP-prone — a higher floor drops low-confidence static-object false animals).

fields.label: Min spawn score — vehicle
fields.description: Minimum score to spawn a vehicle track (FP-prone — a higher floor drops low-confidence false vehicles).

fields.label: Fast high-confidence confirm
fields.description: Let a single very-high-confidence detection confirm a track for events before it reaches the min-hits gate, so a fast subject crossing in 1-2 frames (a passing car) still registers. Off by default (strict N-hit confirmation).

fields.label: Fast-confirm score
fields.description: Score at/above which a detection confirms its track immediately, bypassing min-hits. Only used when fast high-confidence confirm is on.

fields.label: Sub-floor recovery IoU
fields.description: The IoU a sub-floor box needs with a moving tracklet’s prediction to re-attach it. Which boxes count as sub-floor is decided by the "keep tracks through low-confidence frames" option below.

fields.label: Keep tracks through low-confidence frames
fields.description: Boxes below the class confidence floor may keep an EXISTING track alive while the detector is unsure, so a person read at 0.5 for a few seconds keeps one id instead of splitting. They never start a track and never produce events, notifications or snapshots.

fields.label: Low-confidence continuation floor
fields.description: Score at or above which a box the class floor dropped still counts as evidence that a tracked subject is there. Only used with the option above.

fields.label: Record the track history (kept 1 day)
fields.description: Write, continuously, what the tracker is given on this camera — boxes, classes, scores, before the tracker decides — and the ids it produced, never pixels, so a track that went wrong can be promoted and kept as a test case within a day. About 43–72 MB per day per camera on the Artifacts location. Off by default; Events → Debug → Tapes shows what each recording camera costs.

fields.label: Minimum spawn size
fields.description: Require a new track’s box to cover at least a minimum fraction of the frame before it is created — stops tiny far-field / vanishing-point blips from spawning full tracks. An already-tracked subject that shrinks into the distance is unaffected.

fields.label: Min spawn area — person
fields.description: Smallest person box (as a fraction of the frame area) allowed to start a NEW track. 0 = ungated. Conservative default (0.0005 = 0.05% of frame) drops only vanishing-point noise. Raise on cameras with a distant road / horizon.

fields.label: Min spawn area — animal
fields.description: Smallest animal box (fraction of frame area) allowed to start a NEW track. 0 = ungated (animal already has a spawn-score floor).

fields.label: Min spawn area — vehicle
fields.description: Smallest vehicle box (fraction of frame area) allowed to start a NEW track. 0 = ungated (vehicle already has a spawn-score floor).

fields.label: Person/animal group matching
fields.description: Let a detection that flips between person and animal for a frame (a crouching / bending person is often read as an animal) re-match its existing track instead of spawning a concurrent animal track. A flip is the same subject in the same place, weakly read: the cross-class match happens only on the strict predicted-box pass and only for a full-frame box below the "animal over person max score" bar — a confident animal beside a person, or a person beside an animal, is its own subject and keeps its own track. The reported class is still decided by the per-track class vote.

fields.label: Zone membership minimum overlap
fields.description: How much of a detection box must fall inside a zone for the detection to be STAMPED with it — as a fraction of the BOX area, not of the zone. Same bar for live tracks and parked (stationary) occupancy. 0 stamps on any touch, which is what let a plant brushing a zone by 6% fire a "person on the doorstep" rule. Only a stamped zone can match a zone-scoped notification rule. Read the "zone membership stamped on event" log line to choose the value: it prints the achieved percentage per zone.

analytics.title: Stationary objects
analytics.description: Parked / idle object suppression — keeps a stopped car from re-spawning tracks and re-flooding events. Per-device overrides on each camera. Defaults match today’s behaviour.

fields.label: Suppress parked objects
fields.description: Promote a stopped object to a lightweight registry entry and suppress its detections from re-spawning tracks. Off = every parked object keeps spawning normal tracks on this camera.

fields.label: Suppress IoU
fields.description: Overlap at/above which a detection is the SAME parked object (unmoved) → its spawn is suppressed. Lower can suppress genuine new tracks near a parked object.

fields.label: Wake / associate IoU
fields.description: Minimum overlap for a detection to be treated as a parked entry’s OWN object (confirm or wake it). Too low lets a passing object wake a parked entry (re-flood); too high can miss the real departure.

fields.label: Session stillness window
fields.description: How long (ms) a tracked object must stay put before it stops holding a motion session open. It creates nothing: a parked object becomes an entry by being seen repeatedly in the same place, not by one track surviving this long.

fields.label: Observed-time TTL
fields.description: Retire a parked entry after this much OBSERVED (frames-flowing) time without a confirming detection — the object was removed while watched, or a long occlusion.

analytics.title: Stillness scale (per camera)
analytics.description: How slowly a subject has to move on THIS camera before it counts as settled. A camera looking down a 30 m driveway and one watching a doorway two metres away disagree about this by more than an order of magnitude, so one fleet-wide number cannot be right for both. Leave it at 0 and the camera behaves exactly as it always has (a flat 2 px-per-update bar). Run the `stillness.calibrate` action to measure it from the camera’s own recorded tracks — the run reports what it measured and REFUSES, with a reason, when the evidence is too thin.

fields.label: Stillness speed bar
fields.description: Centroid speed, as a fraction of the subject’s OWN box diagonal, per second, at or below which the subject is not travelling. Subject-relative, so perspective is already divided out; per second, so an irregular on-motion cadence cannot masquerade as speed. 0 = not calibrated (the shipped absolute bar decides, exactly as before). Live reference: 0.0136 on a close, mostly-parked view; 0.3081 on a far view whose subjects only transit.

fields.label: Last calibration
fields.description: What the last run measured, from how many samples and tracks, and what it chose — or which named reason it refused for. Display only.

fields.label: Calibrate from this camera
fields.description: Measure this camera’s own recent tracks and WRITE the bar above from them. It refuses — with a reason, and without writing — when the evidence is too thin: no tracks, too few tracks, too few samples, or no movement to scale against. The reading it took is left in “Last calibration” either way, so a refusal is as legible as a result.
fields.confirmMessage: Measure this camera’s recent tracks and overwrite its stillness bar with what they show?
